REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL — Leadership and safety training programme for operational staff
Port of Easthaven Authority (fictional) · PEA-LD-2026-02

1. Introduction
Port of Easthaven Authority (fictional) invites proposals for: leadership and safety training programme for operational staff.
Scope: Design and delivery of a blended leadership programme for 120 supervisors and a refreshed safety-awareness course for 900 operational staff, with an online learning platform and impact reporting over 2 years.

2. Timetable
Clarification questions close: 2026-11-23 at 17:00
Proposal submission deadline: 2026-12-07 at 12:00
Shortlisted bidder presentations: 2026-12-15
Proposal validity: 90 days after the submission deadline
Planned programme launch: 2027-03-01
All times are local time at the buyer's offices. Late proposals will not be considered.

3. Evaluation criteria
Proposals will be scored against the criteria and weightings below. Quality questions are scored from 0 to 5 and then weighted.
Q1 — Programme design and learning approach — 30% — Structure, learning methods, alignment with the Authority's competency framework.
Q2 — Trainers and delivery capacity — 20% — Trainer qualifications, sector experience and capacity across shifts.
Q3 — Learning platform and accessibility — 15% — Online platform, accessibility, offline access and reporting.
Q4 — Evaluation and impact — 10% — How learning transfer and business impact are measured and reported.
P1 — Price — 25% — Total evaluated price from the price schedule.

4. Documents to be returned
Bidders shall return the following documents. A proposal missing any mandatory document may be rejected as non-compliant.
- Signed form of tender (Mandatory)
- Technical proposal answering Q1 to Q4 (max 20 pages) (Mandatory)
- Completed price schedule (Mandatory)
- Trainer CVs for the proposed team (Mandatory)
- Sample module outline and materials (Mandatory)
- Accessibility statement for the platform (Mandatory)
- Three client references (Mandatory)
- Sample evaluation report (Optional)

5. Instructions to bidders
Proposals shall be submitted in English through the buyer's e-procurement portal. Email submissions will not be accepted.
Questions shall be raised through the portal before the clarification deadline. Answers will be shared with all bidders without naming the bidder who asked.
Bidders shall not contact evaluators directly during the procurement. Canvassing will lead to exclusion.
The buyer is not bound to accept the lowest priced or any proposal and will not reimburse bid costs.

docs.label: Terms and conditions
pages:
TERMS AND CONDITIONS OF CONTRACT
Port of Easthaven Authority (fictional) · PEA-LD-2026-02

1. Definitions and interpretation
In these conditions, the Buyer means the contracting authority named above and the Contractor means the successful bidder.

2. Contractor obligations
2.1 Intellectual property. Materials created specifically for the Authority shall be licensed to the Authority for unlimited internal use.
2.2 Insurance. The supplier shall hold public liability insurance of at least USD 2,000,000 and professional indemnity of at least USD 1,000,000.

3. Commercial terms
3.1 Data protection. Learner data shall be stored in the agreed data region and deleted 12 months after contract end unless the Authority requests otherwise.
3.2 Payment. Payment is made against agreed milestones within 30 days of a valid invoice.

4. Termination
Either party may terminate for material breach that is not remedied within 30 days of written notice.
5. Governing law
The contract is governed by the law of the Buyer's jurisdiction.

docs.label: Technical specification
pages:
TECHNICAL SPECIFICATION
Port of Easthaven Authority (fictional) · PEA-LD-2026-02

1. Purpose
This specification sets out the minimum requirements for: leadership and safety training programme for operational staff. 'Shall' means a mandatory requirement; 'should' means a desirable requirement that will be considered in scoring.

2. Requirements (part 1)
2.1 Design. The leadership programme shall be mapped to the Authority's supervisor competency framework in Annex B, with learning outcomes for each module.
2.2 Delivery. Face-to-face sessions shall be delivered on site in groups of no more than 16 participants, scheduled around 24/7 shift patterns.
2.3 Delivery. The safety-awareness course shall be available as a 45-minute e-learning module and as a classroom session for staff without regular computer access.

3. Requirements (part 2)
3.1 Trainers. Lead trainers shall hold a recognised training qualification and have at least 5 years' experience in operational or industrial settings.
3.2 Platform. The learning platform should meet recognised web accessibility guidelines (WCAG 2.1 AA) and work on mobile devices.
3.3 Platform. Completion records shall be exportable to the Authority's HR system in CSV format at least monthly.

4. Requirements (part 3)
4.1 Evaluation. The supplier shall evaluate the programme at reaction, learning and behaviour levels and report results quarterly.
4.2 Languages. Safety materials should be available in plain English and in two additional languages to be agreed.
4.3 Account management. The supplier shall provide a named account manager who attends a monthly review meeting on site.

kb.title: Past proposal — Coastal Logistics leadership programme
kb.text: Every module starts from the client's competency framework. We map each learning outcome to a competency and agree the map with the client before any material is written.

kb.title: Delivery model for shift workers
kb.text: Workshops run on site in groups of 12 to 14, at times that fit early, late and night shifts, including sessions at 06:30 and 22:00.

kb.title: Blended safety course
kb.text: Our safety essentials course runs as a 40-minute mobile-friendly e-learning module or as a facilitated classroom session for teams without computer access.

kb.title: Trainer team
kb.text: All lead trainers hold a recognised adult-training qualification. The proposed team averages 11 years of experience in ports, logistics and manufacturing.

kb.title: Platform accessibility statement
kb.text: The learning platform was independently tested against WCAG 2.1 AA in 2026 and works on phones, tablets and desktops, with offline download for mobile users.

kb.title: HR integration
kb.text: Completion records can be exported as scheduled CSV files or through an API, daily, weekly or monthly.

kb.title: Evaluation framework
kb.text: We evaluate at four levels: reaction, learning, behaviour and results. Behaviour change is checked with line managers 90 days after each cohort.

kb.title: Translation process
kb.text: Safety content is written in plain English first, then translated by professional translators and checked by a native-speaking subject expert.

kb.title: Insurance summary
kb.text: Public liability USD 5,000,000; professional indemnity USD 2,000,000.

kb.title: Licensing terms
kb.text: Bespoke materials are licensed to the client for unlimited internal use; our generic course library remains our property and is licensed per learner.
